questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being in Europe. I wanted to go somewhere I could reach without plane.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy. Although I did feel it was a little difficult to navigate in the many different emails from both host and home university. Especially because I had received info from my home univserity over almost a full year.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a very nice introduction day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started searching on the WG gesucht app. I wrote many, many messages but everytime I got in contact with someone i was offered a place. So I suggest sending out many messages, and setting up video meetings. I went to Berlin with two other friends from home, so we found a place together just for us. But it is also possible to find shared housing on WG.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's not a bad idea. It's compulsory to get a student travel card which means you can use public transport within Berlin unlimited. So easy to get back and to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have no idea.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy, but the system was not so good. You had to meet up at the university, and wait to come into a room where the same person gave the same message to each student over and over again. It took a lot of time and could have been done much more efficiently.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: as explained above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could reach out on email to the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was a great place. Classes were super small (at least compared to what I was used to) which was very nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were rather similar to my home university, maybe a little easier exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different. Much smaller classes and more interactive teaching. For example, I had to prepare two presentations for 3 out of my 5 courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied immigration and cultural economics
Applied Informatics for the Management of Decentralized Energy Systems
Empirical Research in Economics
European Economic History II (1914 - up to now)
Network Based Energy Systems (SoSe 2023)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of the courses and found them all super interesting. Applied immigration and cultural economics was however a very demanding course, which I think you should be aware of. Super interesting but required much more than any of the other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wasn't aware that I had to pay the around 2000 kroner for attending school. The fee included free transport all over Berlin though.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: There is a super cheap canteen at school where all students and staff eat. It was really nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were  many different sport activities offered at really good price etc. but I didnt have the time to do it unfortunately.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try the sports I heard good about them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Berlin has so many different things to offer. Whether it be restarurants, bars, clubs, museums etc. Also really good fleamarkets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There's a student organisation called HUGS which organizes events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be aware semester is shifted
2) Start looking for housing in good time
3) Enjoy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being away and experiencing new things after 4 years at KU.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
